title: How Will the Blue Wave Change State Governments? Send Us Your Questions
author: Ask Bolts
content:
Beyond Congress, the blue wave on Nov. 3 changed the balance of power all
around the country. Democrats won unified control of six new state governments
and ended GOP rule in major states that Republicans have run for decades, such
as Georgia and Texas.

Those results have already transformed the policy landscape in these states.
The new Democratic majorities could pass laws reshaping voting, sentencing,
abortion, labor, school vouchers, and so much more. Plus, the new Democratic
governors will have executive powers to flex, from appointing judges and the
heads of state agencies to decisions over pardons.

Already, these shifts have renewed talk that states could circumvent the
electoral college via a national popular vote compact. More states could
emerge as a bulwark to Trump’s mass deportation agenda, on top of the states
that have already limited local collaboration with ICE. Lawmakers are expected
to consider new restrictions on data centers, new protections for abortion,
and easier ways to register to vote. Plus, it remains to be seen how the
midterms change the frenzy of gerrymandering we saw over the last year.

Now we want to hear from you: What questions do you have on the results of the
midterms and what they mean for possible transformations in state governments?

We know you’re always keen to figure out who holds power and what they’re
going to do with it. So we’d love to hear what you have in mind in light of
these striking midterm results.

Are you wondering what new realities these state elections brought about? What
does it mean for your state to have a new party in control? What policy
avenues do the outcomes open for issues you care about?

Let us know in the form below by **Wednesday, December 2**. And remember: All
questions are welcome. Nothing is too in the weeds for _Bolts_!

And our team will be responding to your questions before the end of the year!
